In this paper, the potential capability of the sectored antenna array for DOA (direction-of-arrival) estimation is investigated. Measurements will be presented for an 8-element array in the 2 GHz band. The antenna array is characterised in terms of input return loss, array mutual coupling and azimuth complex radiation pattern. The issues concerning mutual coupling between the array elements is also discussed. Furthermore, the paper presents measurements made using the array with our parallel channel chirp sounder at UMTS frequencies to estimate DOA information.

articleTitle: Microstrip antenna circuit model and linear pattern correction
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Mutual coupling, among other effects, causes the element patterns in an antenna array to be different. In the practical adaptive use of the array identical element patterns are usually expected. Linear pattern correction with matrix multiplication can be used to correct the array element inputs/outputs. In this paper, a multiport model for a microstrip array and a method to find the input circuit for its ports is presented for use in the array correction.

articleTitle: Application of transient Ultra Wide Band measurement to characterise radiation pattern of automotive antennas
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This measurement set-up permits antenna characterisation without requesting anechoic chamber. The locating of parasitic contributions due to the environment is easier. The effects of these contributions can be eliminated or minimised by time windowing. The time gain is significant for a multi-frequency study.

articleTitle: The effect of magnetic dipole terms on the computed properties of printed-disk transversely-modulated artificial dielectrics
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: The scattering characteristics of artificial dielectric made of a finite cascade of planar lattices of printed disks is analyzed using a self-consistent theory of interaction between the small metallic disks and the associated electromagnetic fields. Previous analyses based on the same theoretical technique did not include the effect of the induced magnetic dipoles; only the induced electric dipoles were considered. In this paper we show that the magnetic dipole effects are noticeable but relatively small. In addition, we use the complete theory to obtain new results on the effects of lattice dimensions on the transmission and reflection behaviour of the m = 0 and m = -1 Floquet modes.

articleTitle: DOA system with synthesized virtual planar array using eigenvectors
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a method of DOA estimation using eigenvectors and evaluated the proposed method by performing simulations and experiments in an anechoic chamber. DOA was estimated correctly in these simulations, and the effectiveness of the proposed method was confirmed. We evaluated the average of estimation errors to be about 1.4° in the anechoic chamber. These results confirmed that the proposed method provides an effective DOA estimation. Further studies are attempting to apply the proposed method to uncorrelated waves and estimate DOA from certain base stations through experiments.

articleTitle: Inverse characterisation of antennas by equivalent sources using spherical harmonics
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present a new synthesis method based on spherical harmonics optimization. In previous works, this method has shown a remarkable effectiveness for E-field estimation around real base station antennas which are formed as linear array. The presented work extends our method to the modeling of some antennas which are different from the classical base station antenna. By testing a Yagi antenna we realized a general model able to synthesize other antennas which are different from linear array. Furthermore, an economical model is developed to improve the efficiency of the general model.

articleTitle: Conformal antennas using 2D and 3D metallized foam technology
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Nowadays, most of microwave applications require antenna conformation and by the way curved surfaces. Low weight, low cost and user-friendly are the other ones. As a solution the laboratory has developed a new technology based on metallized foam. This new technique offers several advantages and new possibilities in the design of 2D and 3D antennas. In order to demonstrate these abilities, several examples dealing with filar, flat and finally 3D antennas are provided and discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Laminated waveguide as radiating element for phased array with brick architecture
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper presents the study of a five-element array antenna prototype developed for communications in K-band. The radiating elements are radiating waveguides realised in laminated technology. The element exhibits a 1 GHz bandwidth around a 20.7 GHz centre frequency. The radiation patterns indicate a gain of 2.7 dBi. In an array configuration the input impedance of each radiating element is slightly perturbed by the proximity of the other antennas. The coupling between the elements, however, remains below -18 dB across the bandwidth. The simulated boresight radiation pattern of a five-element array is stable over the bandwidth and the gain reaches 9.2 dBi at 20.7 GHz. The scanned radiation patterns obtained by simulation show a good behaviour of this array for scan angles up to 50°.

articleTitle: New concept of a reconfigurable EBG antenna
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper presents the principle of a tunable EBG antenna. Thanks to an adapted material it is possible to switch the working frequency. Simulation results of two static structures are presented. The first one will be tested in cavity and we are waiting for the manufactured structure and for the experimental tests. The second will be tested in antenna and has been built. Experimental tests are in progress.

articleTitle: Coherently Radiating Periodic Structures (CORPS): A new perspective of designing antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: The new concept of Coherently Radiating Periodic Structures, CORPS, has been presented. In this case, it has been applied to the design of antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Dielectric-loaded flat reflector test antenna for submillimetre wavelengths
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: An offset dielectric-loaded flat reflector antenna has been designed and realized for submillimeter wavelengths. The antenna has an aperture size which provides a compromise between a high directivity and a reasonable size for a test object in the development work of antenna measurement techniques dedicated for high-gain antenna tests. The diameter of the dielectric loading on top of the flat main reflector is 120 mm and it is made of Teflon. To facilitate the manufacturing, the other surface of the dielectric loading is spherically shaped. The shape of the dielectric loading is optimised by adjusting the ray path lengths equal in the horizontal centreline of the antenna aperture. The ray path lengths are calculated with ray-tracing method. The antenna operation is verified at 310 GHz; the measured half-power beamwidth is 0.51°.

articleTitle: Efficient calculation of green's function integrals for single-layered microstrip structures using complex image
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: In this paper, the effects of t vector for GPOF approximation of a Green's function for a single layered microstrip structure have been evaluated. In order to do this, effects of T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and dt variations and also the simple polynomial profile of non-uniform sampling strategy have been evaluated. The best value for each computation can be determined separately using different compromising policies between time and accuracy.

articleTitle: Thickness reduction of unidirectional spiral antennas
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper presents different solutions allowing the thickness reduction of unidirectional spiral antennas without compromising their broadband properties. First, the effects of adding a ground plane to the radiating element are analysed. Then, the microstrip spiral antenna is loaded by chip resistors, the antenna exhibits a good circular polarization over a 3:1 bandwidth with a thickness of 0.02λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>. In a following part, the spiral antenna is placed 0.013λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub> above a lossy ground plane, a good impedance matching and circular polarization are achieved over a 9:1 bandwidth. Finally, the spiral antenna is implemented on an EBG substrate, the thickness is 0.1 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>, the bandwidth is limited to 70% but this solution leads to a high efficiency antenna.

articleTitle: Terahertz performance of integrated double-slot antennas
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: We present the terahertz performance of integrated lens antennas consisting of a double-slot planar feed antenna and a synthesized elliptical lens. The radiation pattern and the impedance of the planar feed are computed using the method of moments; the collimating action of the lens is modeled using the physical-optics approach based on the Huygens principle. In the frequency range from 1.5 to 3 THz the measured antenna efficiency and radiation pattern correspond fairly well with the results of simulations approving this simulation technique as a reliable tool for the antenna design.

articleTitle: A new approach to the integration of series and shunt coplanar stubs
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper presents the design of new folded-stub matching networks in coplanar technology. Two examples are discussed that show how series and shunt matching stubs can be combined together to reduce the overall size of the structure. Simulation results of a shunt C, series L matching component are presented and compared with measurements.

articleTitle: Annular Slot Antenna with 3-order radiation pattern diversity
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper proposes a new triple Annular Slot Antenna (ASA) system with separate Transmit (Tx) and Receive (Rx) accesses allowing 3-order radiation pattern diversity. Such an antenna is designed for Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) applications in the 5 GHz upper band. A prototype of the antenna system has been designed, realized and tested. Experimental results agree well with theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Feed location effects on miniature microstrip patch antennas bandwidth
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This study was performed on slot loaded microstrip patch antennas. Slots reduce antenna resonant frequency and are used for antenna miniaturization. However, as the antenna size is reduced, the feeding becomes more difficult, and input impedance becomes more sensitive to the feed location. In this paper the effects of feed location on input impedance and bandwidth of two types of slot loaded patch antennas are investigated.

articleTitle: A generalized admittance matrix formulation based on the Electric Field Integral Equation for the fast analysis of dielectric loaded waveguide filters
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Dielectric loaded waveguide filters are extremely attractive for space applications, thanks to the reduction of size and weight that can be achieved using these components. Another remarkable advantage is the high temperature stability and the high quality factor of the recent dielectric materials, allowing in many cases these products to be the optimum choice for the filter realisation in comparison with the conventional hollow waveguide filters.

articleTitle: MDS in the analysis of pre-fractal printed strip gratings
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: In this paper, we present new method for the modeling of printed strip gratings. Our general approach for finite perfectly electric conducting (PEC) strip gratings printed on a dielectric substrate with a PEC ground plane is based on the parametric representations of the integral and pseudo-differential operators and Method of Discrete Singularities (MDS). Diffraction problem is first reduced to hypersingular integral equation. Then this equation is solved using the MDS. Finite-order Cantorian set strip grating is investigated numerically. Some of obtained results are presented.

articleTitle: The properties of microstrip patch antennas with EBG substrates within the lower frequency band outside the bandgaps
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Microstrip patch antennas with EBG substrates within the lower frequency band outside the bandgaps are studied. Initially, the bandgaps of a two layer EBG structure are found. Then, patch antennas are designed to work just below the bandgap. By a parametric study for two layer EBG antennas, it is found that very wide impedance bandwidths of up to 21.08% can be achieved together with a higher gain of about 10 dBi. The performance of the reference patch and single layer EBG patch are also given for comparison.

articleTitle: The merits of Analytical Regularization and Analytical Preconditioning
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Summarizing, by using the MAR/MAP it is possible to overcome many difficulties encountered in conventional MoM treatments. Theoretical merits of the MAR are numerous: exact solution existence is established, convergence is guaranteed, and rigorous asymptotic formulas can be derived. Computationally, the MAR results in a small matrix size for a practical accuracy, and sometimes no numerical integrations are needed for filling in the matrix. Thus, the cost of MAR algorithms is low in terms of both CPU time and memory. A frequent feature is that both power conservation and reciprocity are satisfied at the machine-precision level, independently of the number of equations, whatever it is. As (I+A)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> is bounded, the condition number is small and stable, not growing with mesh refinement or increasing with the number of basis functions. The latter fact means that conjugate-gradient numerical algorithms are very promising even in spite of a possible squaring of the condition number, as has already been emphasized in [9]. Using fast iterative methods, applied to the MAR matrix equations with static-part inversion, it is probably possible to perform an accurate full-wave desktop analysis of the Arecibo reflector. However, the same thing can be done more economically by using a high-frequency inversion.

articleTitle: Reflectarray with integrated band reject filter for MEMS based beamforming applications
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: A microstrip reflectarray is a low profile antenna consisting of an array of radiators illuminated by a feed as shown on Fig. 1. Beamforming techniques and performances have been widely studied to improve spherical wave to plane wave transformation using patches of variable sizes for instance [1,2], or stub loaded patches [3], or variable slots in ground plane [4]. These approaches are based on the same principle: having elementary antennas with identical reflection magnitude but controlled reflection phase. Any incident and reflecting configurations can be realized, limited by elementary antenna radiating performances.

articleTitle: A novel fast method for accurate Modal analysis of the Microstrip Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Numerical Methods for analysis and design of Microstrip Patch Antennas (MPAs) are time-consuming and quality properties about the analyzed structures are not appropriately achieved using them. Multiport Network Model (MNM) is considered as one of the best models for analysis and design of these Antennas. This model includes several circuit networks, each representing one characteristic of the Microstrip Antenna. In this paper, a novel, fast and accurate method for Modal analysis of two MPAs is presented using the MNM. The results reveal the frequency, type and number of the patch resonance modes in each frequency interval. Also, it is possible to discern the modes excited by some feeding port(s). Furthermore, with analysis of the achieved results at different modes, a new and deep insight for the MPAs' operation is accrued.

articleTitle: A new equivalent junction model for characterizing power absorption by lossy scatterers in reactive field regions
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper provides a new method to characterize power absorption mechanisms in reactive field regions. According to the proposed approach, the energy dissipated in any lossy scatterer exposed to any radiating source is described in terms of power transfer from a set of equivalent generators to a microwave junction. By introducing the concepts of available power and load factor in electromagnetic fields, this general and analytical model allows a better understanding of near-field energy deposition phenomena and identification of the most impacting parameters. In order to illustrate the relevance of this technique, the equivalent junction model is applied to the full analysis of power absorption in a lossy cylinder close to a current line source.

articleTitle: Astigmatic beam tracing hybridised with FDTD for on board antenna analysis
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: An hybrid FDTD-ABT scheme has been proposed for the electromagnetic field analysis of an on board antenna. The hybrid method resorts to a spherical wave expansion to link the FDTD code to the ABT code, i.e. spherical harmonics are used to provide ABT with a suitable description of the source modelled with FDTD. This approach exploits the ability of FDTD to treat detailed models of the antenna and its nearby structures while ABT is able to perform the analysis of the satellite environment.

articleTitle: A well-conditioned formulation of 1D inverse scattering problem under the Born approximation
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: A new methodology for robust imaging of permittivity profiles in 1D inhomogeneous media is proposed. The image reconstruction technique makes use of non-local orthogonal basis functions that span the entire remote image region. The linearized integral equation is weighted at different frequencies which yields a diagonally dominant matrix due to the orthogonality of the kernel and the specially selected set of the basis functions. The condition number of the matrix corresponding to the discrete form of the integral operation exhibits no variation with the dimension of the discrete space. Excellent results were obtained for the reconstruction of a dielectric slab having both continuous and step-like permittivity profiles using only a few basis functions. The method exhibits robustness under a wide variety of experimental conditions and constitutive parameter profiles. The new formulation allows for a straightforward generalization to multi-dimensional imaging problems.

articleTitle: Miniaturized “Dark Eyes” antenna for pulsed microwave sensing: Complete microstrip-fed design
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: In this work, we reported on an antenna design with a complete microstrip feed suited for near-field microwave imaging centered at 6GHz. The antenna is compact and has a planar structure. Future work will be directed toward studying the antenna efficiency and fidelity for different values of surface resistivity. In addition, the antenna will be studied in an array configuration for near-field imaging applications.

articleTitle: Traveling electromagnetic waves on linear metallic nanosphere arrays
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: The analysis of full-wave dipole coupling, by means of the vector spherical-wave source scattering-matrix approach, successfully predicts the k-β diagrams for traveling waves on linear periodic arrays of lossless metallic nanospheres.

articleTitle: Accurate 2-D model of planar antenna based on finite reflection grating fed by a dielectric waveguide
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: The accurate 2-d model of radiation of the electric modes of a PDW on finite number of rectangular grooves cut out on the surface of the perfectly conductive screen have been built for the first time.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband signal transmission using integrated dipole antennas in silicon integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Ultrawideband (UWB) signal transmission in Si integrated circuits was performed by use of wireless interconnects. Linear dipole antennas fabricated on a Si substrate showed UWB characteristics in the frequency range of 5-20 GHz. The signal attenuation rates of Gaussian monocycle pulse through 10 Ωcm and 2.29 kΩcm substrates were -0.08 mV/chip and -0.03 mV/chip, respectively. Pseudo random binary signals were transmitted and received between Si chips and the lowest bit error rate of 128 bit binary signal with 13.5 Gbps was 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>. Interference of Gaussian monocycle pulses transmitted from a dipole antenna could be suppressed by use of differential mode signals instead of common mode signals.

articleTitle: An improved microwave imaging system exploiting a multi-source-illumination strategy
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Microwave imaging techniques are aimed at reconstructing an unknown region under test starting from the measurement of the scattered electromagnetic field. In such a framework, this work focuses on an innovative strategy that fully exploits the information arising from the illumination of the investigation domain with different probing sources. To point out the potentialities of the new approach, some results of a comparative study with single-source methodologies are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Design of a self-matched dual-frequency coplanar waveguide-fed-slot antenna
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper presents two new designs of dual frequency coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed double folded slot antennas. This includes both conductor backed and non-conductor backed CPW that radiate into a half space or full space, respectively. An important advantage of these antennas is that each is self-matched to 50 Ω CPW feed line without the need for external matching circuit. This reduces the antenna size and simplifies its design. To verify the designs, the return loss and radiation patterns are obtained using different commercial software, which employ different full wave methods.

articleTitle: Small short-circuited antennas fed by electromagnetic coupling
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Two small short-circuited antennas of λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/11 and λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/8 have been designed and measured. Their respective bandwidths of 120 MHz (2.3 %) and 190 MHz (3.6 %) make them suitable for 4G telephony applications. An array of two miniature antennas has also been built. Its performances show that it is appropriate for MIMO applications.

articleTitle: Local optimization of mm-wave integrated lens antennas
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: A design methodology of optimized homogeneous dielectric lens antennas is proposed. The procedure comprises two successive stages. Geometrical Optics (GO) principles are firstly implemented to determine the best lens profile that radiates a specified amplitude-shaped output pattern. Then this GO solution serves as an initial condition to optimize the lens shape using an analysis kernel based on the standard diffraction integral. For that purpose, the optimizer uses a multi-dimensional Conjugate Gradient Method with Ribiere-Polak parameters for a fast convergence of the algorithm. Experimental results obtained at 58.5 GHz with non-optimized and optimized Teflon lenses successfully validate our modelling tools for the analysis, the synthesis and the optimization of arbitrarily-shaped 3D single refractive surfaces.

articleTitle: Broadband power detector using a circularly-toothed planar logarithmic-periodic antenna
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: A broadband antenna has been coupled to a planar Schottky diode for the realisation of a sensitive power detector for mm-wave frequencies. The measured response curve is in agreement with calculations and shows values of up to 3000 V/W. However, further work has to concentrate on the accuracy of the sensitivity and the reduction of ripples in the frequency response. Also higher frequencies are targeted and characterisation at THz-frequencies has to be performed.

articleTitle: Time-domain analysis of lossy-substrate interconnects with frequency-dependent parameters
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: The use of semiconductors as substrate in microwave devices is becoming more common in the design and implementation of low-cost integrated circuits. The presence of a lossy substrate and the loss-reduction techniques, through modification of the interconnect geometry, result in significant frequency dependence of the per-unit-length (p.u.l) parameters of the transmission line. In this paper, an approach is presented for time-domain simulation of transmission lines implemented on a Si substrate. We use a finite-element method to extract the p.u.l parameters (as functions of frequency) for a given interconnect which has been fabricated over a low-resistivity Si substrate. A time-domain recursive convolution technique, based on approximating the transmission line parameters using Vector Fitting algorithm, is used to analyze the interconnect. We present a method to integrate the proposed approach within a general-purpose circuit simulator. This allows the simulation of interconnects terminated with arbitrary linear/nonlinear networks. Some simulation results are presented to show the capabilities of this method.

articleTitle: A fast auto-adaptive method to study the frequency behavior of radiating structures, applied to automatic determination of resonances
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Solving electromagnetic scattering and radiation problems with moment methods or finite element methods over a large frequency band gives accurate results, but it is often too time-consuming. So we propose a fast auto-adaptive method to optimize the computational electromagnetics solver applied in the case of various radiating and dielectric structures. This method is able to generate the electromagnetic behavior of the antenna with a very few simulations over a broad frequency band.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable phased-arrays based on hybrid couplers in reflection mode
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper presents the design of antenna arrays of patches fed by microstrip hybrid branchline couplers in reflection mode as phase shifters. This topology permits the reduction of the number of FET, PIN diode or MEMS switches by two when compared with classic array feeding techniques. Two antenna prototypes are simulated, fabricated and measured. The results show beam steering capability over a 400 MHz band centered on 5.8 GHz with good matching performances.

articleTitle: Localized defects and random variations in 3D-PBG
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: The object of our study is to use photonic band gap structures (PBG) in the conception of materials with specific electromagnetic properties in microwave frequency range: absorbing, scattering or transparent materials. The main domains of applications are Electromagnetic Compatibility or uperstrates of antennas.

articleTitle: MEMS switching circuits for reconfigurable space communication systems
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: In this paper, basic MEMS switching networks fabricated on alumina substrate have been presented. Such devices could be used to design multiple input-output switching matrixes able to select and steer RF signals to satellite smart antennas for example. For their low loss, low power consumption and high linearity, MEMS switches appear to be particularly well suited for these applications. This paper also presents an original approach with MEMS switching function integration and packaging directly with others circuits fabricated on the same wafer. This approach should permit to develop high efficiency and limited cost switching networks for space applications.

articleTitle: Sources for total-field/scattered-field formulation in FDTD simulation using approximations to dispersion equation
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: A full set of numerical wave number k that includes imaginary part as function of frequency can now be obtained by a simple procedure which does not involve numerical root-finding scheme. FFT computation and data storage for the entire time sequence of all fields along the grids can also be avoided by approximating frequency domain inverse transform. The results of the initial numerical simulation are encouraging but are limited by the numbers of terms in the derivative expansions. Other numerical approximations are being investigated and these will be the focus of the presentation.

articleTitle: Using multiple antennas in UWB communications
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Extensions of traditional Single-Input Single-Output (SISO) UWB systems to Multiple Elements Antennas (MEA) at both ends of the links (MIMO: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output) are investigated. The mutual coupling in arrays of UWB biconical antennas and the radiation patterns are analyzed in time domain from measurement data in frequency domain. The contribution of MEA in UWB communications is evaluated in terms of Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) gain from measured radio channel in Line Of Sight (LOS) and Non Line Of Sight (NLOS) environments.

articleTitle: Broadband plate-loaded monopole antenna on a dielectric substrate
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Wideband top-loaded monopole antenna on a dialectric substrate was proposed, and design method using the decomposed model was presented in this paper. Parameter study to assist the antenna design was also carried out by using the MoM calculation.

articleTitle: Design of a GSM, DCS and UMTS adaptive beam steering base station antenna
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: The goal of this paper is to present a beam steering multi-band base station antenna for mobile communications without RF components (phase shifters, amplifiers, ...) or Butler matrix. This base station antenna associates a omni-directional antenna to a cylindrical controllable metallic Electromagnetic Band Gap (EBG) material. The main characteristic of this lattice is to include PIN diodes along the metallic wires in order to control the conductivity of each wire and so the angular sectors where the cylindrical EBG structure is transparent. After a presentation of the controllable EBG material and the beam steering principle, we will present the passive antenna that have validate the principle and the simulated EM performances before the active one with 1080 diodes and we will show the EM performances of this kind of structure. A part of the works presented here have been made under the RNRT “BIP” project [1].

articleTitle: Multilayer antenna array in Q band for spatial communications
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper deals with a multilayer printed antenna array. This study takes place in European MIPA project [1] concerning an antenna prototype which is apart of Q band (50 GHz) one-feed-per-beam antenna reflector. In millimetre waves, it is highly required to separate active layer (MEMS, MMIC, ..) and radiating elements to avoid electrical spurious generated by coupling radiation. This separation is done with a very thick metallic support (2 mm). Moreover, this thick ground plane is important for thermal dissipation aspect. In this aim, the authors present an original feed of antenna array via a H shape thick slot transition. Results of antenna array radiating patterns, power gain and efficiency are given in the considering bandwidth (47.2 to 50.2 GHz).

articleTitle: Dielectric and metallic Electromagnetic Band Gap antennas for omnidirectional coverage of telecommunication networks
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper presents omnidirectional metallic EBG (Electromagnetic Band Gap) antennas. The composition of the structure is explained and some typical radiation patterns in the principal planes of the antenna are shown. The performances of the antenna in terms of directivity and radiation bandwidth are defined function of the EBG material composition and of the height of the antenna. Finally, a comparison between dielectric and metallic EBG antennas is presented in order to bring to the fore the advantages of metallic structures.

articleTitle: Split Ring Resonators and Slot Split Ring Resonators: Influence on microstrip line transmission and possible applications
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: The study that is done in this paper compares the physical phenomena observed when placing a 50Ω microstrip line on respectively a periodic lattice of SRRs and a SSRRs defected ground plane. In both cases, a band-stop phenomenon is observed, but the coupling with the microstrip line is completely different. When using SRRs, there is a weak magnetic coupling since the magnetic field of the line does not fully penetrate through the SRRs. Whereas, when using SSRRs in the ground plane of the conducting line, the coupling is mainly electric due to the strong capacitive coupling created between the line and the inter-SSRRs metal.

articleTitle: Antenna developments for EMBRACE, the European demonstrator program for SKA
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Within the framework of the Square Kilometer Array, the Thousand Element Array has demonstrated the aperture array concept for radio astronomy. To confirm the feasibility of aperture array antenna technology for radio astronomy an array with an aperture equivalent to a 25 m reflector antenna will be constructed (EMBRACE). The antenna design of this array must be cost-effective and at the same time deliver high performance results. This necessitates the use of mass manufacturing technologies and low-cost RF substrates. The accurate characterization and design of such an antenna will require both commercial and specially developed antenna modeling tools. Alternative element designs should minimize production costs and avoid high loss transmission lines. The design will be performed using a combination of infinite and finite array formulations. Tight integration of the electromagnetic and mechanical design disciplines should lead to a mass producible design, maintaining the high performance required for radio astronomy.

articleTitle: Dielectric resonator antenna with dual linear polarisation and orthogonal excitation
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper presents a novel structure with dual polarisation and orthogonal feeding. The radiating element is a dielectric resonator antenna (DRA). It constitutes a very compact source suitable for active arrays. The simulated results are presented at 4.5 GHz. At that step, a large bandwidth, a low cross-polarisation and a high isolation between polarisations are demonstrated.

articleTitle: A ground penetrating radar antenna with improved shield
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: In this paper, development of an improved antenna for short-range ground penetrating radar (GPR) applications s discussed. the antenna improvement is obtained in the form of increased radiation efficiency and reduced dimension. In addition, an improved metallic shield has been designed not only for protection against EMI and antenna coupling, but also for strengthening radiation into the ground.

articleTitle: A Ka-band 37-element reflective spatial power combiner
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: A reflective spatial power combiner employing the tile architecture is presented. This spatial power combiner is to be used as part of a dual-reflector transmitting antenna intended for uplink satellite communications at Ka band. A modular array composed of 37 elements is to be fabricated and intended to provide more than 20 W of output power with a combining efficiency of 58%.

articleTitle: Performance metrics for UWB antennas
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: With the desire for ever-increasing data-rates, coupled with the interest in techniques that offer interference mitigation, much research has focused upon Ultra Wide-Band (UWB) systems that can theoretically realise such benefits. In practice, any UWB system will require an antenna to connect it (the radio) to free-space. Through examples of practical measurements from two different UWB antennas, this paper will discuss the characteristics that must be considered when assessing UWB antennas.

articleTitle: Active radiating antennas using an oscillator circuit
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper describes the association of an oscillator loop circuit with multi-layers microstrip antennnas. A design procedure is outlined and the performances at 24 GHz of two prototype circuits are reviewed.

articleTitle: Radiated and guided waves in planar dipole arrays
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: In this theoretical study eigenfields of a periodical arrangement of longitudinally directed dipoles on an infinite plane are considered. The dipoles are small wire antennas, which are close to each other forming an infinite dipole array. The coupling between the antenna elements is taken into account. An analytical solution for waves propagating along this dipole array structure is considered. Radiated and guided-wave solutions are possible depending on the properties of the loaded dipole scatterers. This kind of structure can be used as a planar leaky wave antenna.

articleTitle: Novel external smart antenna array for IEEE 802.11a wireless LAN applications
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Design and simulation of a smart antenna system for 802.11a wireless LAN is proposed. The main advantage of this design is that it is applicable as an external antenna module, regardless of the other parts of the system i.e. the WLAN card. The antenna is a 3×3 planar array of rectangular patches, in the 5.15GHz ∼ 5.35GHz band. The antennas are probe-fed so that they can be connected to separate phase shifters or switches. Suggestions have been made to make use of a minimum number of phase shifters. Simulations include all possible mutual coupling effects. A switched-beam algorithm is applied to single user, double and triple user environment. A minimum 15 dB increase in the received signal gain and 5 dB increase in SIR are achieved. In a reduced mode of the smart array using only 4 phase shifters, at least 3 dB increase is observed in SIR.

articleTitle: Multilevel fast Physical Optics algorithm for reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: A multilevel fast physical optics (FPO) algorithm for computation of the radiation patterns of reflector antennas via hierarchical domain decomposition is presented. The multilevel computation essentially reduces to the aggregation of radiation patterns of increasingly larger sub-domains, starting with the direct evaluation of radiation characteristics of small radiating sub-domains and ending with the whole reflector. Numerical results demonstrate that even with a simple cubic interpolation the proposed FPO approach provides a large speedup without degrading the accuracy of the resulting radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Direction of arrival and time of arrival measurements using five-port reflectometers and quasi-Yagi antennas
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: A new system based on five-port reflectometers, which measures simultaneously direction of arrival (DoA) in azimuth plane and propagation time of arrival (ToA) of incoherent signals and coherent signals for indoor communication applications is presented in this paper. The receiver operating at 2.4 GHz consists of seven five-ports and a Uniform Linear Array (ULA) of seven quasi-Yagi antennas. The data processing method is also presented. Estimation procedure for joint DoA and ToA is based on the Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm associated with Spatial Smoothing Pre-processing (SSP). The simulation and experimental results show that the signals are well estimated.

articleTitle: 60 GHz electromagnetic fields do not activate stress-sensitive gene expression
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: The purpose of this study was to determine whether millimeter waves exposure at 60GHz, upcoming to use for indoor high rate communications in local area networks, could lead to a stress response in human brain cells. U-251 MG cell line was sham-exposed or exposed to low power density millimeter radiation for different duration, from 1h to 33h. Using the transfection technique, we analyzed the gene expression for reporter genes previously shown highly sensitive to many environmental insults. We have tested the influence of 60GHz radiations on 3 different gene expression systems, overlaying the main cellular response pathways to physical and chemical stresses. No statistically significant difference was detected in transcriptional activity of reporter genes after radiation exposure. These results suggest that radiation in the frequency range around 60GHz is not a stressor strong enough to modify the stress-sensitive gene expression.

articleTitle: Hologram based compact ranges for antenna and RCS testing at submm waves
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Compact ranges based on amplitude and phase holograms have been developed and shown to be applicable at submillimeter wavelengths. Amplitude hologram based compact range has been successfully used for measuring a 1.5 m reflector antenna at 322 GHz. A phase hologram based compact range has been demonstrated for RCS measurements at 310 GHz.

articleTitle: Novel wide-band half hemispherical dielectric resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: A symmetrically half section of a hemispherical dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) has been studied and proposed as a novel broadband antenna. The input return loss characteristics, associated resonant modes and their field patterns and the radiation characteristics over the operating band of a probe-fed DRA have been investigated using Ansoft HFSS solver. Suitable radiation patterns with nearly 40% bandwidth (S11<;-10dB) have been obtained from a single element low profile DRA structure.

articleTitle: 5GHz indoor OFDM system using 4-element array antenna with analog phase shifter
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: 5GHz band wireless LAN system in indoor environment suffers from multi-path distortion. It causes an attenuation of received power and frequency selective spectrum distortion. In this paper, we describe an array antenna system with analog phase shifter that has the robustness for the multi-path distortion. The proposed array antenna system is low cost and is not complex in the control circuit. We evaluate the error rate performance of OFDM system using our array antenna system by the computer simulation and the experimental measurement in indoor wireless LAN system. The computer simulation uses the channel frequency response based on the result from ray tracing. We specify our array antenna system only controls the direction of carioid beam pattern, and we compare our system performance with the performance of antenna selective diversity. The indoor experimental results show our system has better packet error performance with small footprint.

articleTitle: RCS characterization using wavelet analysis
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Application of wavelet signal processing techniques to radar target cross section (RCS) identification is a very promising strategy to achieve high recognition level for any type of complex target. Capabilities and limitations of wavelet techniques have to be taken into account when applied to these recognition problems and these major issues are addressed in this paper using practical targets.

articleTitle: Formal expressions for the solution of Dirichlet and Neumann problems
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Based on the relationship between the potential and its normal derivative on the boundary of the region of interest, the solution of the Dirichlet and the Neumann boundary value problems relative to the Laplacian is written explicitly in an operator form. The numerical computation of the potential for regions of arbitrary shape is performed by converting the two boundary operators involved into square matrices, which only depend on the boundary shape. The formulas presented are of interest since they allow a direct calculation of the potential in a given region under any Dirichlet or Neumann boundary conditions. These solution formulas represent for regions of arbitrary geometry what the direct integration Green formulas represent for some canonical regions for which the problem-specific Green functions can be constructed analytically.

articleTitle: The analysis of ultra wideband wheel microstrip patch antenna using non-uniform photonic bandgap substrate structure
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: The characteristics of new ultra wideband (UWB) wheel microstrip patch antenna using non-uniform photonic bandgap (PBG) substrate structure has been analyzed using a full 3D electromagnetic field inside a structure based on the finite element method. The UWB technologies have been developed to exploit a substantially new spectrum resource and to realize ultra high-speed communication, high precision radar, and other sensing systems. The antenna has UWB approximately in range of 1 MHz to 20 GHz and its performance above 20 GHz is sensitive to the gap position in the ground plane. These gap positions enhance some modes and weaken others, which have been used to control the antenna bandwidths up to 31.4 %. The proposed antenna is constructed on ground plane of thickness 0.1 mm and FR-4 epoxy substrate of thickness 1.6 mm with relative permittivity 4.4. The radiation characteristics for the designed antenna such as return loss, input impedance, near field, radiation pattern and 3D-polar radiation pattern with respect to changes on the air gap position in the ground plane are obtained using numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Nonradiative dielectric (NRD) waveguide to rectangular waveguide transition in millimetre waves
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: The authors present a nonradiative dielectric (NRD) waveguide to rectangular waveguide transition which operates in the millimetre wave band. The aim of this transition is to match systems in NRD technology to standard rectangular waveguides. Simulation and measurement results, in term of return and insertion losses, are presented in two frequency bands: 30 – 40 GHz and 45 – 55 GHz. This transition will then enable to feed millimetre wave functions, enabling to design feed structures for antenna arrays, especially multibeam.

articleTitle: European R and D on millimetric antennas and integrated antennas within the ACE Network of Excellence
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: The ACE Network of Excellence brings together 45 of the antennas groups in Europe with the aim of improving the research collaboration and interaction across Europe. The activity area on millimetric antennas and integrated antennas involves 12 of these. This paper briefly introduces the operation of the activity in the Network and then overviews the current research and development taking place in the partner institutions.

articleTitle: Circular polarisation design of a triple fed equilateral-triangular microstrip antenna using FDTD
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: A design of triple-feed equilateral-triangular microstrip antenna for circular polarization (CP) is proposed. In this design, by feeding the patch through three points and applying proper phase differences between the feeds, CP with axial ratio close to 1 can be achieved. Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method has been applied to analyze this microstrip-fed antenna. The return loss, input impedance, far field pattern, and axial ratio are calculated and compared with the same results which are derived by HP-HFSS software.

articleTitle: Antenna Q-factor computation with FDTD method
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: In this work, we have developed a new method for the calculation of the antenna quality factor by using the numerical method FDTD. The results obtained with our method are compared with the analytical approach of McLean and Geyi. The results show good agreement between FDTD and Geyi formulation.

articleTitle: Structure transformation effects on the radiation characteristics of a low-profile spiral-loaded monopole antenna
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: The analysis reveals the radiation characteristics for transformed spiral arms. It is found that a VSWR frequency bandwidth of 11.4% is obtained for a transformation ratio of b/a = 0.67. Within this frequency bandwidth, an almost constant radiation pattern is obtained with a gain of approximately 5.2 dBi.

articleTitle: Simulink implementation of a CDMA MIMO-beamforming system
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper presents the Simulink implementation of a Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) beamforming system based on the code filtering approach (CFA) and Alamouti's transmit diversity. This model can be used as a platform to test the use of DSPs/FPGs in new generation of MIMO-beamforming systems and will allow evaluating the Bit Error Rate (BER) and the beampattern performances. This goal is achieved through modeling and simulation using the rapid prototyping environment based on Mathworks Simulink. Simulation results show that the proposed hybrid beamforming CFA and space-time coding technologies significantly outperform MIMO systems without beamforming.

articleTitle: Applications of coaxial-slot antenna for interstitial and intracavitary microwave hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper describes the applications of the coaxial-slot antenna to the interstitial and intracavitary microwave hyperthermia. First, we confirmed the effectiveness of the treatment by use of our developed antenna. Next, the investigation of the heating performances of the coaxial-slot antenna for treatment of bile duct carcinoma was shown and the possibility of the treatment was described. As a further study, we will have much more cases of actual treatments by the interstitial microwave hyperthermia and will study the antennas for intracavitary heating aiming at practical use.

articleTitle: Millimetre wave antenna research at Helsinki University of Technology
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper describes the research work at the Radio Laboratory of Helsinki University of Technology concerning millimetre and submillimetre wave antenna technology: development of new antenna designs and, especially, development of antenna measurement techniques for electrically large, high-gain antennas. Also, development work of some related fields in millimetre wave instrumentation is presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of conformal antennas in spheroidal geometries: A mapping into planar components
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: In this contribution, we apply the mapping between conformal antennas in complex geometries and planar equivalent antennas loaded with complex materials [F. Bilotti, A. Alù, L. Vegni, PIER 47, 1 (2004)] to the case of spherical and spheroidal geometries. Even though the complexity of the problem is not reduced after this rigorous mapping, a generalization of the Method of Lines (MoL) numerical algorithm can then be applied successfully. Starting from the generalized transmission-line equations that relate the transverse electromagnetic field components in a generic linear material embedded in a given orthogonal non-planar reference system, it is possible in fact to apply a 2-D discretization on the transverse plane, leading to a system of coupled differential equations for the line samples of the field. The theory and some numerical results are presented and discussed, showing the capabilities of this technique in terms of efficiency and accuracy, and underlining how a wise employment of non-conventional media may lead to interesting improvements of the radiating features of common microwave conformal antennas.

articleTitle: Technological sensitivity of nonintuitive GA Optimized printed antennas
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: In this article, several GA Optimized antennas with nonintuitive shapes are fabricated and measured. The technological sensitivities for the different realized prototypes are compared. This study points out the high technological sensitivity of antennas with unconventional geometries. The results of this study give rules allowing to directly reject from the optimization process the structures which are too sensitive.

articleTitle: Discussion on the definition of the antenna radiation Q
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: According to the classical theories developed by Chu, Wheeler and subsequent authors, there exists a fundamental law which restricts the performances of antennas enclosed in a given volume. This law states that the antenna radiation quality factor Q (proportional to the ratio of time-average non-propagating energy to radiated power) cannot be smaller than the one obtained if only the lowest spherical order mode is excited out of the minimal sphere containing the antenna. However, some authors have recently contradicted this lower limit of Q, exhibiting antennas overcoming this bound. This paper shows that the contradiction mainly relies on a problem of formulation of the quality factor, resulting in a different definition of Q, compared with the classical one. Nevertheless, this raises the question of the interest of using other expressions of Q, depending on the parameters of the problem to be optimized. In fact, it is shown that, if the goal is to obtain the largest matching bandwidth or efficiency, then the Q factor should not be considered at the frequency point of balance between the electric and magnetic stored energies, as it is classically done. It would rather be calculated at the frequency where the reactive power is null (the antenna is matched) which is generally not equivalent to the stored energies balance for complex multi-mode antennas.

articleTitle: Exact analytical solution for the losses in and forces on an induced conducting spheroid
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: An analytical solution is presented for the induced currents in highly conducting prolate and oblate spheroids due to the presence of an external axisymmetric inducing field produced by carrying-current circular turns. Exact analytical expressions are derived for the magnetic vector potential, the power losses and the forces acting upon the spheroids. The magnetic vector potential outside and inside the conducting spheroids is determined by solving the vector Laplace equation and the vector Helmholtz equation, respectively, using the method of separation of variables.

articleTitle: Null generation using far field parasitic element
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: If a suitable parasitic element position in far field of an antenna, it can produce a well-designed null in an arbitrary direction of a general antenna. Using acceptable simplifications, analytical results describe this phenomenon approximately. This method is general for all type of antennas. This method has been used to suppress the pattern of a two-element array antenna. The simulation results show tolerable coordination with analytical solutions.

articleTitle: Phase tunable ground plane defect array
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: An electrostatically actuated membrane structure placed behind a multiple defected ground structure, is shown to provide between 20° and 40° in differential insertion phase from 10GHz to 20GHz when compared to a reference transmission line. The measured characteristics of the unbiased membrane structure are shown to differ slightly from the reference line.

articleTitle: Performance of adaptive beamforming arrays for spatial interference rejection
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper analyzes the performance of LMS and RLS adaptive beamforming algorithms used in smart antenna systems for spatial interference rejection. Multiple criteria are used to evaluate these beamforing algorithms including number of incident signals and their angular separation, number of array sensors and their spacing. Results of numerical simulations are useful for the design smart antenna systems with optimal performance.

articleTitle: Design of a multi-source EBG antenna for diversity of polarization
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: It has appeared very easy to design a circularly polarized EBG antenna using a patch antenna with notches. The results meet to our wishes. The use of several feeds under the EBG material allows to radiate a left or/and a right circular polarization with the same EBG antenna.

articleTitle: Some new capabilities in GRASP9
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: In 2004 TICRA released the new version of GRASP, GRASP9. A lot of new features have been added to those present in the predecessor, GRASP8. Two of those features, analysis of gaps in reflector surfaces and parallel processing, will be described in this paper.

articleTitle: Design of an integrated antenna for automotive applications
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Due to specific requirements for automotive applications, the design of an integrated antenna system able to guarantee the connection to several wireless services, i.e. GPS, GSM/GPRS and COSPAS-SARSAT, must be faced as an optimization problem. Starting from electrical and geometrical constraints, the design of the antenna must be faced considering, in addition to usual antenna design procedures, also interferences phenomena arising from the integration of antennas belonging to different classes in a single compact device. In the paper are described the design phases of the device and the experimental and numerical validation activity conducted on a prototype of the antenna.

articleTitle: Cold-cavity lasing spectra and thresholds of two optically coupled microresonators with whispering gallery modes
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: Any laser is a complicated electron device governed by joint action of the transport of carriers, stimulated emission of photons, heating, and optical field confinement. To respond a challenge of comprehensive modeling of semiconductor laser, one needs full account of all these mechanisms. However, a reasonable reduction of complexity of the analysis can be achieved within so-called “cold-cavity” problem viewing optical modes as solutions to electromagnetic theory equations with appropriate boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Phased array developments: An overview
publicationTitle: 11th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics [ANTEM 2005]
abstract: This paper gives an overview of developments and projects in the area of steerable antennas (phased array) at IMST. Through the years, this type of antenna has become a key area within IMST and various projects have been conducted in the past, and are currently ongoing. Phased array antennas incorporate in general active components for beam steering, and have achieved ever more popularity during the last years, mainly driven by mobile multimedia applications. It is intended to give here an impression of the work performed, thus a global overview and not a detailed technical description. For further information it is referred to more specific publications.
